content.text:
Here's what I found.

## 1. Existing admin-user server actions (`src/actions/auth.ts`)

Only two exist there:

```ts
export async function listUsersAction(email?: string, limit?: number)
export async function setAdminRoleAction(userId: string, isAdmin: boolean)
```

- `listUsersAction` — `requireAdmin()` then delegates to `listUsersActionCore` (`src/lib/core/auth/auth.ts`). Supports email-substring search or a `limit`-bounded listing.
- `setAdminRoleAction` — `requireAdmin()`, calls `setAdminRoleActionCore`, then **does** `revalidatePath('/footy/admin/users')`, `revalidatePath('/footy/admin/user', 'layout')`, and `broadcast(FootyChannel.Users)`. This is the one action used today, wired from `AdminUserList`'s per-row `Switch`.

No ban/unban, delete-user, resend-verification, or revoke-session actions exist for admin use. Related but distinct code:
- `src/actions/verifyEmail.ts` (`verifyEmail`, `sendEmailVerification`) is a self-serve flow (email verification tokens), not an admin action against another user.
- `deleteUser` (better-auth API) is invoked from `src/lib/core/deletePlayer/deletePlayer.ts` as a side effect of deleting a *player* record — there's no standalone "delete this auth user" admin action/button anywhere.
- No ban/unban action exists at all, despite `UserWithRolePayload` carrying `banExpires`.

So if SYS-560 wants role-change/ban/delete/resend-verification actions on this page, only role-change has a matching server action today; the rest would need to be built from scratch (core function + action with `requireAdmin`, `revalidatePath`, `broadcast`).

## 2. UI conventions for admin actions elsewhere

- **`src/components/AdminUserList/AdminUserList.tsx`** — table with sortable headers (`UnstyledButton` + `IconSortAscending/Descending`), `TextInput` filter, and a `Switch` per row for the one binary action (grant/revoke admin), wired straight to `setAdminRoleAction` with try/catch → inline red `Text` error. Row name/email link to the per-user page via `Anchor href={/footy/admin/user/${encodeURIComponent(user.email)}}`.
- **`src/components/AdminPlayerList/AdminPlayerList.tsx`** — richer pattern: `Checkbox` multi-select with select-all/indeterminate, `SegmentedControl` filters, a grouped action bar (`Group` of `Button`s, e.g. "Onboard N player(s)", disabled when no selection), an "Impersonate" `Button` per row (disabled if no linked user id), and `@mantine/notifications` `notifications.show/update` for loading → success/error toast feedback instead of inline text. No `Menu`, `Modal`, or `Badge` here.
- **`src/components/UserButton/UserButton.tsx`** — the one place using Mantine `Menu`: `Menu.Dropdown` with `Menu.Label` sections ("Account", "My Data"), `Menu.Item` with `leftSection` icons, `Menu.Divider` between groups — this is the closest existing template for "logically grouped, clearly labelled admin actions."
- No confirmation-`Modal`/`useDisclosure` pattern exists anywhere in the codebase (checked `Modal` and `window.confirm`/`useDisclosure` usage — only unrelated hits in `GameResultForm`, `Turnout`, `CustomAppShell`, table components). So there's no established "confirm before destructive action" convention to copy; one would need to be introduced (e.g., Mantine `Modal` + `useDisclosure`) if adding a delete/ban action.
- `Badge` usage exists only in unrelated components (`ClubBadge`, etc.) — no status-badge convention (e.g., "Banned"/"Verified") used in admin lists today.

## 3. Is the single-user page reachable from a list, and is the JSON dump a regression?

- Yes — `AdminUserList.tsx` links both the name and email cells to `/footy/admin/user/${encodeURIComponent(user.email)}`, so it is reachable as a "view details" action from `/footy/admin/users`.
- Git history (`git log --follow -p`) shows `AdminUserData.tsx` has **always** been a raw JSON `CodeHighlight` dump since its creation in commit `0016084d` ("SYS-475 Refactor user page to server component; add AdminUserData component and related tests"). That commit converted the page from a client component into a server component + extracted `AdminUserData`, but even the pre-refactor client version it replaced was already just `Title` + `CodeHighlight(JSON.stringify(user))`. Subsequent commits (`c975885d`, `194cb4cd`, `d83ff608`) only did import-path/type/React.FC cleanups — no functional change. So this is not a regression from some richer prior UI; it has been a debug/dev-view since day one and was never built out into a real admin-actions page.

## 4. FootyChannel.Users wiring

- `broadcast(FootyChannel.Users)` fires only inside `setAdminRoleAction` (the only mutating action touching users).
- `<AutoRefresh channels={FootyChannel.Users} />` is correctly rendered on both `/footy/admin/users/page.tsx` and `/footy/admin/user/[email]/page.tsx` — so the plumbing/convention (revalidatePath + broadcast + AutoRefresh) is correctly followed for the one action that exists.
- Any new actions added for this page (ban, delete, resend-verification) will need to follow the same pattern: `requireAdmin()` → core mutation → `revalidatePath('/footy/admin/users')` + `revalidatePath('/footy/admin/user', 'layout')` + `broadcast(FootyChannel.Users)`, matching `setAdminRoleAction`'s existing shape.

## Bottom line for SYS-560

The single-user admin page currently exposes **zero** admin actions — no buttons, menu, switch, or badge, just a `Title` + full raw JSON (`CodeHighlight`) of the `UserWithRolePayload` object inside `Container > Paper > Center`. That JSON dump has been present since the component's creation as an apparent debug/placeholder view, not a deliberate deliberate design choice reached after some richer UI. The checklist item "Admin actions are clearly labelled and logically grouped" is **not satisfied** on this page today: the only grouped/labelled admin actions in the app live in `AdminUserList` (Switch) and `AdminPlayerList` (button group + notifications), and neither pattern nor any server action for role-change-with-context, ban, delete, or resend-verification has been implemented on this per-user page.
